questions.q: What does the number after the slash in CIDR notation, like the /24 in 192.168.10.0/24, represent?
options: The total number of devices allowed on the subnet
How many of the address's 32 bits make up the network portion
The subnet's priority level for routing
The number of subnets in the entire organization
questions.explain: The CIDR number states how many of the 32 address bits are the network portion; the remaining bits are host bits that determine the subnet's size.

questions.q: Why does a /24 subnet provide 254 usable host addresses instead of 256?
options: Two addresses are always reserved: the network address (all host bits zero) and the broadcast address (all host bits one)
IPv4 only allows 254 devices per network by law
Two addresses are reserved for the ISP
questions.explain: Usable hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2, because the all-zeros network address and the all-ones broadcast address are both reserved and not assignable to devices.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail split its network into separate subnets (warehouse, corporate office, guest Wi-Fi) instead of one flat network?
options: Flat networks are illegal under networking standards
It contains broadcast traffic, allows different security rules per group, and prevents a problem on one subnet from affecting another
Subnets make every device's IP address permanent
It is required for every network to have at least two subnets
questions.explain: Subnetting contains broadcast traffic to the group that needs it, lets different security policies apply per subnet, and isolates problems (like excessive traffic) to the subnet where they occur.

questions.q: Northbridge's warehouse has about 40 devices with room to grow to 55. Why is a /26 (62 usable hosts) a better fit than a /27 (30 usable hosts) or a /24 (254 usable hosts)?
options: A /27 is too small to fit current and future devices, while a /24 wastes far more address space than the warehouse needs
A /26 is required by Northbridge's ISP contract
There is no real difference between any of these options
A /24 is always the correct choice for any subnet
questions.explain: A /27 can't fit 55 devices (only 30 usable hosts), while a /24 offers far more addresses (254) than needed. A /26 at 62 usable hosts fits comfortably with room to grow, without excessive waste.

questions.q: In the subnet 192.168.10.0/26, what is the broadcast address?
questions.explain: A /26 has 6 host bits (64 total addresses, .0 through .63). The broadcast address is always the last address in the range, all host bits set to one: 192.168.10.63.
